$comment: Reactor Bot workplaces (user 2026-11-02, Option 1 of docs/worker-types-study.md): the workplace worker-type toggle reads Beaver | Bot | Reactor Bot, and the three are exclusive (Bot workplaces take ordinary bots only, Reactor Bot workplaces take Reactor Bots only). Every workplace in the game can be set to Reactor Bots, including beaver-only and specialist-only ones. The District Center's default worker type has the same third option. Runtime: src/DeepFrontier/Scripts/SuperBots/ReactorBotWorkplace*.cs. Written by tools/reactor_bot_workplace_content.mjs (the colour, the singleton and the localization rows); checked by tools/validate_reactor_bot_workplaces.mjs.

illumination.$comment: Window light while the workplace is set to Reactor Bots (only Reactor Bots work there): an IlluminatorColorizer above the native bot blue (WorkerTypeIlluminator, priority 20) and below the player's own colour (CustomizableIlluminator, 100). Neon green #39FF14; not a player preset (no IlluminationPresetSpec), like the Reactor Bot eye colour.

unlock.$comment: Per-workplace science unlock of the Reactor Bot option (user: 3x the cost of the normal bot unlock). cost = botUnlockMultiplier x the template's native Bot entry in WorkplaceSpec.WorkerTypeUnlockCosts. A workplace with no Bot entry (beaver-only, specialist-only, or bots free) uses the bot unlock Deep Frontier gives its own buildings, its BuildingSpec.ScienceCost + missingBotUnlockAddend (0 science without a BuildingSpec), times the same multiplier: e.g. District Center or a flag 3,000, Nuclear Reactor 3,003,000, Launch Pad 603,000.
